attrs.label: Stalwart URL
attrs.description:
Scheme and host of your Stalwart Mail Server, with no path.</br>
The JMAP session is discovered at /.well-known/jmap under it.</br>
Only this container talks to Stalwart; browsers never do.</br>
Example: https://mail.example.com

attrs.label: App Secret
attrs.description:
A long random string the session keys are derived from.</br>
Generate one with: openssl rand -base64 48</br>
Changing it signs everyone out.

attrs.label: App Name
attrs.description: Branding shown in the UI and reported by the health endpoint.

attrs.label: Image Proxy
attrs.description:
Route remote images in messages through ihasmail, so senders never see your address.</br>
Disable to load them straight from the sender's server.

attrs.label: Secure Cookies
attrs.description:
Auto marks the session cookie Secure when the request arrived over HTTPS, which is what a reverse proxy gives you.</br>
Force it on or off only if that detection is wrong for your setup.

enum.description: Auto (Secure when the request arrived over HTTPS)

attrs.label: Port Bind Mode
attrs.description:
The port bind mode.</br>
- Publish: The port will be published on the host for external access.</br>
- Expose: The port will be exposed for inter-container communication.</br>
- None: The port will not be exposed or published.</br>
Note: If the Dockerfile defines an EXPOSE directive,
the port will still be exposed for inter-container communication regardless of this setting.

enum.description: Publish port on the host for external access

attrs.label: Session Storage
attrs.description:
The only thing ihasmail ever writes: sessions.json, kept so that nobody is signed out when the app restarts or updates.</br>
Nothing else of yours lives here. Mail, settings, calendars and contacts all stay in Stalwart.

1.0.0.readme:
ihasmail

ihasmail is immutable webmail for Stalwart Mail Server: mail, calendars, contacts, files and filters in one app, talking only JMAP. It needs a Stalwart 0.16 or newer that it can reach, and keeps nothing of its own beyond an optional session file.
